entries.title: Release 26.12.0
entries.details:
#### Features

- [#9559](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9559) Add the Amethyst theme to the custom theme catalog — thanks @geogabrielp
- [#9347](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9347) Add a Quarterly interval to custom reports — thanks @kareemhalabi
- [#9547](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9547) Add the Tokyo Night theme to the custom theme catalog — thanks @williamcorsel
- [#9343](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9343) Add server support for creating and revoking API keys for individual budgets — thanks @jfdoming
- [#9345](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9345) Create and revoke API keys for individual budgets from Security settings — thanks @jfdoming
- [#9344](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9344) Allow scripts to download and update selected budgets using a separately revocable API key — thanks @jfdoming
- [#8878](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/8878) Add an "is between" option to date and amount filters. The filter is inclusive for both start and end values. — thanks @DavidGrinberg
- [#9432](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9432) Add one-off withdrawals to the Monte Carlo report so a lump sum such as a house deposit or pension tax-free cash can be taken at an age — thanks @MikesGlitch
- [#9426](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9426) Make Akahu bank sync (New Zealand banks) available to everyone without enabling an experimental feature — thanks @MatissJanis
- [#9620](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9620) Enable Banking bank sync for European banks is now available to everyone — thanks @MatissJanis

#### Enhancements

- [#9509](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9509) Add a mobile Tags page for adding, editing, filtering and deleting tags — thanks @matt-fidd
- [#9382](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9382) Add haptic feedback to the keypad, swipe actions and pull to refresh in the iOS and Android apps — thanks @MatissJanis
- [#9271](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9271) Add a hidden setting to try the new browser storage engine, and move the API's browser build to it so pages using it no longer need cross-origin isolation headers — thanks @MikesGlitch
- [#9260](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9260) Add `applyCategoryTemplate` and `getCategoryTemplateAmount` to the API to budget a category from its templates — thanks @nowak-mariusz
- [#8981](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/8981) Add support for managing dashboard pages and widgets through `@actual-app/api`. — thanks @andycarlberg
- [#9485](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9485) Allow API keys to sync SimpleFIN and Pluggy accounts using credentials configured for the budget — thanks @jfdoming
- [#9486](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9486) Add an option to allow API keys to sync shared bank connections — thanks @jfdoming
- [#9293](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9293) Automatically extend budget planning beyond 12 months, up to 5 years ahead, in Envelope and Tracking modes. — thanks @x-rous
- [#9405](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9405) Add an "Average of previous weeks" budget automation — thanks @tim-smart
- [#9208](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9208) Show the largest scheduled inflows and outflows behind a balance forecast, with links to review and edit each schedule. — thanks @samaluk
- [#9207](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9207) Add balance forecasts that start today, keep saved ranges moving forward, and label today or the current month on the chart. — thanks @samaluk
- [#9517](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9517) Make stacked dialogs faster by only blurring the background of the top dialog — thanks @RandomSpaceship
- [#9297](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9297) Show a small ring beside the balance of categories whose goal is not yet funded, which fills as the goal is funded, and stop coloring envelope income categories by goals left from a tracking budget — thanks @mattm4444
- [#9197](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9197) Show the horizontal axis labels on bar and line chart cards in the reports dashboard — thanks @RandomSpaceship
- [#9209](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9209) Compare up to four named balance forecast lines with separate account and transaction filters, and save them to your dashboard — thanks @samaluk
- [#9218](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9218) Move the actions on the payees, tags, rules and schedules pages into a toolbar above the list and give those pages and bank sync a consistent layout — thanks @matt-fidd
- [#9438](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9438) Allow mobile users to copy/paste into the transaction amount field. — thanks @rjinnette
- [#9604](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9604) Mobile: menus and dialogs now glide into place when the on-screen keyboard opens or closes, and no longer slide under the status bar at the top of the screen. — thanks @MatissJanis
- [#9459](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9459) implemented better payee name and bank transfer info parsing for Fineco bank — thanks @guglicap
- [#9383](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9383) Mobile apps: stop registering the web update mechanism, and hide the "new version available" notice and the self-hosting setup hint, since updates and setup work differently there — thanks @MatissJanis
- [#9304](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9304) Show a category's goal as soon as you save its budget automations, without changing the budgeted amount — thanks @mattm4444
- [#9406](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9406) Allow the Reports page to be hidden from the sidebar — thanks @RandomSpaceship
- [#9121](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9121) Improve how quickly the budget appears when opening it. — thanks @aelxxs
- [#9320](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9320) Monte carlo - Load the reports dashboard faster when it has a Monte Carlo card — thanks @MikesGlitch
- [#9093](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9093) Add a button to remove a tag from a transaction's notes when hovering the tag — thanks @rtwfroody
- [#9409](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9409) Reorder report dashboards by dragging them in the dashboard selector — thanks @RandomSpaceship
- [#8862](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/8862) Budget schedules using a smarter forecast that stops adding to a category once it holds what its upcoming bills need — thanks @MikeBishop
- [#9326](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9326) Scroll to and highlight the other side of a transfer when opening it from the transfer arrow — thanks @rapastranac
- [#9540](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9540) Show the setting for trying the new browser storage engine in Experimental settings — thanks @MikesGlitch
- [#9462](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9462) Skip goal template targets whose month has passed instead of failing the whole template run, and stop `by` and `spend` targets from pulling money back out of a category that is already funded beyond them — thanks @e13h
- [#9329](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9329) Make the iOS and Android apps much smaller to download and install. — thanks @MatissJanis
- [#9384](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9384) Sync and re-check the server connection when the iOS and Android apps return to the foreground — thanks @MatissJanis
- [#9633](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9633) Add an accent color to themes. One color now drives buttons, links and selected rows, and custom themes can set it — thanks @matt-fidd
- [#9573](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9573) Check a budget moved to the new browser storage engine against the original before the original is removed, and offer a way back to the previous engine when a move fails — thanks @MikesGlitch

#### Bugfixes

- [#8791](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/8791) Fix an occasional API crash on shutdown while schedules are being processed — thanks @cakeni
- [#9564](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9564) Accept Quicken QIF transaction detail codes during import — thanks @sshnox
- [#9466](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9466) Fix recurring schedules without an assigned account not advancing after being paid — thanks @saiyam-jain-dev
- [#9535](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9535) GoCardless: use the merchant as the payee for Alior Bank credit card payments too, not only debit card payments — thanks @muhimu
- [#9523](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9523) Prevent the background artwork from flickering during updates. — thanks @lfrb
- [#9331](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9331) Fix Crossover report resetting to a blank slate on page refresh by awaiting category and account selection initialization — thanks @grzdev
- [#9263](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9263) Handle Date values when checking the current month or day. — thanks @fallintoplace
- [#9226](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9226) Fix the sync server not starting on systems with IPv6 disabled — thanks @grzdev
- [#9374](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9374) Prevent categories from becoming orphaned when updated with an invalid group ID. — thanks @emadleo13
- [#9554](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9554) Fix Akahu bank sync failing before 1pm New Zealand time and dropping transactions from the first hours of the day — thanks @EnesKartal
- [#9602](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9602) Fix the API's `deleteTransaction` resolving before the transaction is deleted — thanks @montjeffrey
- [#9393](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9393) Show a clear error with recovery steps when the API finds a budget that is out of sync with the server. — thanks @bubbletroubles
- [#9410](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9410) Fix automatic bank sync not running in the iOS and Android apps — thanks @MatissJanis
- [#9470](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9470) Fix the Budget Analysis report counting categories in hidden groups and leaving out overspending from the month before the selected period — thanks @tabedzki
- [#9372](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9372) Mention budgeted amounts in the delete category warning, not only transactions — thanks @vulinh1704
- [#9625](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9625) Fix End of month cleanup budgeting negative amounts when To Budget is negative — thanks @rapastranac
- [#9471](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9471) Fix accented characters appearing corrupted when opening exported CSV files in Excel — thanks @tabedzki
- [#9541](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9541) Respect date filters when calculating averages in custom transaction reports. — thanks @wunsir
- [#9278](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9278) Fix reports added on one device never showing up on your other devices, and bring back any that went missing — thanks @youngcw
- [#9467](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9467) Fix the category donut chart turning black when theme chart colors use hsl values — thanks @Edzard9
- [#9456](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9456) Fix deleted transactions coming back after every sync for some Enable Banking banks — thanks @MatissJanis
- [#9549](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9549) Fix Enable Banking importing pending transactions when that setting is turned off, and marking holds and scheduled payments as cleared — thanks @MatissJanis
- [#9468](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9468) Fix Enable Banking syncs that some banks rejected, or that failed when the bank could not report a balance — thanks @MatissJanis
- [#9454](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9454) Show a clear error when Enable Banking setup fails or its list of banks cannot be loaded — thanks @MatissJanis
- [#9455](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9455) Add dark and tinted iOS app icons and a dark-mode splash screen — thanks @bmuna
- [#9479](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9479) Fix exporting the budget and other files in the iOS and Android apps — thanks @MatissJanis
- [#9592](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9592) Keep popovers and dropdown lists clear of the iOS status bar and home indicator — thanks @NikolaKrtinic
- [#9601](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9601) Keep toast notifications above the mobile navigation bar and iOS bottom safe area. — thanks @EnesKartal
- [#9529](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9529) Fix wrong balances and crashes when linking Pluggy.ai or Akahu accounts — thanks @samjonath
- [#9497](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9497) Stop the search box from covering the add button on the tags, rules and schedules pages at narrow widths — thanks @matt-fidd

- [#9335](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9335) Fix long payee names being cut off in the rule editor on mobile — thanks @vulinh1704
- [#9590](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9590) Fix the mobile selection bar covering the last transaction in the list — thanks @hskl18

- [#9309](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9309) Prevent invalid calculations from interrupting transaction amount editing. — thanks @doksanbes

- [#9576](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9576) Fix the app getting stuck on loading when a budget that failed to open is opened again in the same tab — thanks @MikesGlitch
- [#9402](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9402) Fix custom reports showing unchecked or hidden categories when “Show empty rows” is enabled. — thanks @sraylanka
- [#9566](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9566) Fix reports resetting to their default settings when the on-screen keyboard opens on mobile devices — thanks @thomasjbarrett82
- [#9308](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9308) Fix downloading a report snapshot in Firefox — thanks @pendevster
- [#9579](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9579) Fix reports not loading without an internet connection — thanks @MatissJanis
- [#9212](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9212) Show the running balance when transactions are sorted by date with the oldest first — thanks @kikoval
- [#9613](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9613) Budget a schedule template whose schedule has no amount as 0 instead of failing with "Cannot read properties of null" — thanks @YasinzHyper

- [#9351](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9351) Fix SimpleFIN connection failures on recent nightly builds — thanks @jfdoming

- [#9494](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9494) Fix keyboard focus getting stuck on tables and show a focus outline when a table is focused — thanks @matt-fidd
- [#9502](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9502) Fix tags not updating after undoing a tag change — thanks @matt-fidd
- [#9511](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9511) Make zero and neutral amounts easier to read in all themes — thanks @matt-fidd
- [#9483](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9483) Fix menus and dialogs appearing offscreen on iPhone at higher zoom levels — thanks @jfdoming
- [#9433](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9433) Hide the "Warning" link in the top bar of the iOS and Android apps when the phone is rotated to landscape — thanks @MatissJanis

- [#9609](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9609) Allow swiping from the screen edge to go back in the iOS app. — thanks @MatissJanis

- [#9363](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9363) Keep transactions and running balances after sorting by date while reconciled transactions are hidden — thanks @boutchitos

- [#9328](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9328) Keep the bank sync status pill below the notch in the iOS mobile app — thanks @MatissJanis
- [#9369](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9369) Fix transaction notes with line breaks being rewritten when the notes field is focused — thanks @YasinzHyper

- [#9575](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/9575) Break transfer cycles into net transfer chains to prevent recursion error — thanks @emiltb

entries.title: Release 26.11.0
entries.body:
This release includes automatic bank syncing, reports grouped by tags, and more customisable navigation, as well as numerous other fixes.

- Sync linked bank accounts automatically at a chosen interval while Actual is open
- Group custom reports by tags and choose which tags to include
- Show, hide, and reorder sidebar pages, and choose your start page
- Support for per-budget SimpleFIN credentials
- Optimizations for performance and memory usage on large budget
- Experimental: Add investment phases and a pot balances chart to the [Monte Carlo analysis report](https://actualbudget.org/docs/experimental/monte-carlo-analysis)

:::warning Breaking changes

- If you're running your own custom SimpleFIN bridge on a private network address, you must now configure the [server allowlist](https://actualbudget.org/docs/config#actual_simplefin_allowed_networks-configjson-simplefinallowednetworks) to prevent SSRF attacks. (If you don't know what this means, it probably doesn't apply to you.)
- As of this release we are no longer publishing standalone `.flatpak` downloads on the release page. You can still use Flathub or the AppImage on Linux.

:::

entries.title: Release 26.10.0
entries.body:
This release speeds up transaction editing, makes syncing more resilient to version mismatches, adds an in-app Notifications page, and introduces an experimental redesigned sidebar with account groups, as well as numerous other fixes.

- Speeds up transaction editing, especially in larger budgets
- Adds a [Notifications](https://actualbudget.org/docs/notifications) page to catch up on what's new in each release without leaving the app
- Makes Actual more resilient to version mismatches, improving syncing between devices running different versions
- Improves bank file imports, fixing accented letters (like é or ü) showing up garbled and supporting more CSV formats
- Experimental: Adds a [redesigned sidebar](https://actualbudget.org/docs/experimental/redesigned-sidebar), based on the winning entry from the [sidenav design competition](https://actualbudget.org/blog/sidenav-design-winner), that lets you organise accounts into groups, reorder them by drag and drop, and search them
- Experimental: Adds income streams, a yearly cashflow chart, custom stocks/bonds/cash mixes and much more to the [Monte Carlo analysis report](https://actualbudget.org/docs/experimental/monte-carlo-analysis)
- Experimental: Adds an option to show transfers in the spent view of the [Sankey report](https://actualbudget.org/docs/experimental/sankey-report)

entries.title: Release 26.9.0
entries.body:
This release makes the transaction table customizable, adds an in-app tour for new users and a new experimental retirement report, as well as numerous other fixes.

- Show, hide, and reorder columns in the transaction table with the new column manager
- New users now experience an in-app tour that guides them through getting started
- Rename a [tag](https://actualbudget.org/docs/transactions/tags) from the Tags page
- A new Schedule button lets you schedule future-dated transactions, replacing the "Convert to Schedule" prompt
- Reorder upcoming scheduled transactions by drag and drop
- Experimental: Add a [Monte Carlo analysis report](https://actualbudget.org/docs/experimental/monte-carlo-analysis) that estimates how long your savings will last in retirement
- Experimental: Add four more currencies (Israeli New Shekel, Macedonian Denar, Peruvian Sol, Uruguayan Peso)
- Experimental: Formula reports can use BALANCE_OF, and formula editors now autocomplete loan and investment functions

:::warning Breaking change

This release updated the Node version for our container images to Node 24. This means that we are dropping support for 32-bit ARM in our Ubuntu images. If you are still using this platform, we'd recommend switching to the Alpine image (`:26.9.0-alpine`), which continues to be supported.

:::

entries.title: Sidenav Design Competition: We Have a Winner
entries.body:
The votes are counted, and the [sidenav design competition](https://actualbudget.org/blog/design-competition-sidenav) has a winner: **congratulations to [matt-fidd](https://github.com/matt-fidd)!** 🎉

## One Winner, Many Great Ideas

Picking a single winner was never going to be easy, and the [voting results](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/issues/8642) showed just how strong the whole field was. While matt-fidd's design won the vote, we will likely take ideas from every submission as we build. What this competition really gave us is a clear picture of the look and feel this community prefers, and that's exactly what we needed.

## Free Swag for Everyone Who Participated

A huge thank you to everyone who submitted a design. As a token of our appreciation, **everyone who participated is getting free Actual Budget swag.** I've already emailed all participants with the details, so check your inbox!

## What Happens Next

Now the fun part: turning the winning design into reality. Work on the new sidenav will begin shortly.

**Want to help build it?** DM me on [Discord](https://discord.gg/pRYNYr4W5A) and we'll see how we can break up the work.

One honest note for everyone joining in: some ideas will get rejected, and there will be pushback along the way. Please don't be disheartened. That's a normal part of the design process, and there will be iterations until we release. Every round of feedback gets us closer to a sidenav we're all proud of.

Thank you again to everyone who designed, voted, and cheered from the sidelines. This is what a project built by its community looks like.

The submissions are in and the finalists are picked. Now it's your turn: **voting for the [sidenav design competition](https://actualbudget.org/blog/design-competition-sidenav) submissions is officially open.**

First things first: a huge thank you to everyone who sent in a design! The range of ideas, from careful refinements to complete rethinks, blew us away. Picking the finalists was genuinely hard, and that's the best problem to have.

Whether or not your design made the shortlist, thank you for putting your time and creativity into Actual. This competition only worked because you showed up for it.

We will be getting in touch with the finalists shortly to send out the free Actual SWAG!

Head over to the voting page and add a 👍 reaction to the designs you like best. You can vote for as many as you want. Voting runs for one week, and the top-voted design gets built into the app.

**🗳️ [Vote here](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/issues/8642)**

Want to talk about the designs? Join the discussion on [GitHub](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/issues/8643) or in the [#project-design-system channel on Discord](https://discord.com/channels/937901803608096828/1345447799319429160).

## A Word About This Community

Moments like this remind me why I love volunteering my time on Actual. This project is built by its community, for its community. Watching it grow, seeing the passion people pour into everything from code to designs to helping each other out on [Discord](https://discord.gg/pRYNYr4W5A), is the most rewarding part of it all.

Thank you for being part of it.

entries.title: Design Competition: Reimagine the Actual Budget Sidenav
entries.body:
The sidenav is one of the most-used parts of Actual Budget. It's how you jump between your budget, reports, schedules, and accounts; and it's the first thing you see every time you open the app. We think it's time to give it some love, and we want the community to lead the way.

So we're running a design competition. **The top 10 designs get free Actual Budget swag, and the winning design gets built into the app.**

## What We're Looking For

We want fresh thinking on how navigation in Actual Budget should look and feel. There's no single "right" answer. We're interested in seeing a range of ideas, from subtle refinements to bold rethinks.

A few things worth keeping in mind as you design (these are constraints, not a checklist):

- The sidenav has to handle the core navigation: budget, reports, schedules, payees, rules, settings, and bank sync, alongside the list of accounts (incl. closed).
- The account list is open-ended. Some people have three accounts, some have thirty. On-budget and off-budget accounts need to be distinguishable, and account balances are often shown inline. Bank sync status is also crucial.
- It needs to work across light and dark themes (and our other color themes).
- Accessibility matters: keyboard navigation, focus states, and reasonable contrast.
- AI usage is allowed.

## How to Enter

Submit your design through this form:

**🎨 [Submit your design here](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScSpvSX6QE-HjiVo3PxkmLLCxVfVfetgL2u8LDBz6YU8lHGdg/viewform)**

You can submit **as many designs as you like.** If you have three different directions, send all three as separate entries.

Polished Figma files are welcome but not required. A clear annotated mockup is perfectly fine.

## Timeline

- **Submissions open:** 27th June, 2026
- **Submission deadline:** 27th July, 2026
- **Public voting:** approx 3rd August, 2026
- **Winner announced:** shortly after voting closes

## How It Works

1. **Submit** your design(s) through the form before the deadline.
2. **We shortlist internally.** After the deadline, the maintainers will review every entry and pick the strongest designs — up to **10 finalists.**
3. **The community votes.** The finalists go up as GitHub issues, and anyone can vote by reacting (👍) to their favorites. Voting runs for one week.
4. **The winner gets built.** The top-voted design will be implemented into Actual Budget.

## Prizes

- **The winning design gets implemented** in Actual Budget. Your work will be shipped to everyone who uses the app.
- **Everyone in the top 10 gets free Actual Budget swag.** Make the shortlist and we'll send something your way.

## Voting

When the finalists are announced, each design will be posted as a GitHub issue. To vote, just add a 👍 reaction to the designs you like best. We'll tally reactions at the end of the voting week.

We'll share the direct links to the voting issues here and in our community channels once the shortlist is set.

## Questions?

If anything's unclear, ask in the [Actual Budget Discord community](https://discord.gg/pRYNYr4W5A). We can't wait to see what you come up with.

Happy designing!

entries.title: Next Steps for Funding Contributors
entries.body:
Over the last few months, our system for compensating core contributors has proven effective. We've built a sustainable foundation that recognizes the invisible labor that keeps the project running. Now, it's time to look ahead.

## Expanding Rewards Beyond Core Maintenance

While the current program rewards essential maintenance tasks (reviews, triage, releases), we want to broaden our scope. The next step is to reward the people doing the work that moves the project forward — fixing bugs, implementing features, and improving the user experience.

## The Ideal: Targeted Donations

In a perfect world, we'd enable donors to fund specific issues or features directly. Someone could say, "I'll donate $50 toward fixing this bug," or "I'll help fund this feature I really want."

At this time, **OpenCollective doesn't offer targeted donations**, and previous third-party tools designed for this purpose have either been discontinued, changed direction in problematic ways, or mismanaged funds. To avoid potential risks and additional administrative overhead, we're not pursuing targeted donations right now. That said, we'll keep evaluating this option and revisit it if a reliable solution becomes available in the future.

## A Practical Alternative: Points for Feature Work

If targeted donations aren't possible, the next best approach may be to extend our existing points-based system **for core maintainers**. Each merged pull request could earn the author a fixed number of points. This approach encourages contributors to submit smaller, more focused pull requests rather than large, hard-to-review ones.

At the end of each month, we'll calculate the points earned by each contributor from all eligible activities—including merged pull requests, code and docs reviews, and triaging issues. Each person's payout will be proportional to their total points out of everyone's combined score for the month. To reflect the broader range of rewarded work, we're **increasing our monthly funding pool from $1,000 to $2,000**.

This model keeps things transparent and simple while rewarding real work from across the community.

## Funding all contributors

There's strong interest in compensating everyone who contributes meaningful work. However, we also have a valid concern that broad payments might encourage low-quality or superficial pull requests. We need to find a balance between being open to more contributors and maintaining quality.

## Steps we plan to take:

Donating a portion of funds to **upstream projects** or **well-maintained plugins** that our project depends on.

Using a **nomination-based system** (similar to how we distribute swag) to recognize and reward active contributors.

## For non-maintainers:

Consensus is leaning toward **nominations** and **issue bounties** rather than tracking every single contribution.

There's an open question on how to **implement bounties efficiently** without adding heavy administrative overhead. We're open to hearing all ideas in this domain!

---

## Share Your Thoughts

We'd love to hear what you think. Does this direction make sense to you? Should we move forward with it?

All feedback is welcome — your input helps shape how we fund and sustain this project.

entries.title: Reflecting on Your 2025 Finances
entries.body:
As we step into 2026, it's natural to look back at the year that just passed. While many apps send you a "year in review" at the end of December, we thought it would be fun to create something special for Actual Budget users — a way to reflect on your financial journey throughout 2025.

## Introducing Actual Budget Wrapped 2025

We've built a small web app that helps you visualize your financial story from the past year. [Actual Budget Wrapped 2025](https://wrapped.actualbudget.org) takes your Actual Budget data and transforms it into a personalized financial recap.

Whether you want to see your biggest spending categories, track your income trends, or simply marvel at how many transactions you've managed — this tool gives you a different perspective on your financial data. Sometimes it's helpful to step back and see the bigger picture of where your money went throughout the year.

The app is designed to be simple and privacy-focused. Your data stays in your browser and is processed locally. We don't collect or store any of your financial information — it's just between you and your Actual Budget file.

## Why Reflect?

Looking back at your finances can be eye-opening. Maybe you'll discover patterns you weren't aware of, or perhaps you'll be pleasantly surprised by how much progress you've made toward your goals. Maybe you'll spot areas where you can improve, or celebrate wins you've forgotten about.

Personal finance isn't just about numbers on a screen — it's about the choices we make, the goals we set, and the progress we track along the way. Sometimes taking a step back helps us appreciate how far we've come.

So head over to [wrapped.actualbudget.org](https://wrapped.actualbudget.org) and take a few minutes to see your 2025 financial story. We hope it brings you some insights, or at the very least, a moment of reflection as you plan for the year ahead.

Here's to making 2026 another great year for your finances!

entries.title: Roadmap for 2026
entries.body:
Hello Actual Budgeters!
Another year has gone by with many fixes and upgrades to Actual.
Let's look back over the year and also look at what's to come.

## 2025 in review

It's always fun to look back and see all the progress made in Actual over the course of a year.
It's easy to forget how many of the features we love weren't available back at the beginning of the year.

### New features

My favorites in approximately chronological order are:

- OIDC and multi-user support
- Adjustable upcoming time frame for schedules
- Multiple new report types
- NPM package for the sync server
- Translations
- Bank sync management page
- Desktop app improvements such as the embedded server
- Auto-hold income
- Merge transactions
- Transaction tags
- Mobile pages for Rules, Payees, Schedules, and Bank Sync
- Budget Currencies (still experimental)
- Quickly add single schedules from the account view

**Note on Translations:** Translations are a never-ending project.
Every month there are new or modified strings that need to be translated.
We could use as many contributors to translation as we can get.
If you are interested in helping translate Actual into other languages see [our translation guide].

If you remember our roadmap from last year, you will see that we were able to accomplish all but one of our goals, plugins.
I will touch on that more below.

### Maintainer and contributor payments

This year we started paying small stipends to the core maintainer team, and giving out SWAG items to other contributors.
The maintainer stipends are based on points received for doing the necessary, but not very exciting, parts of maintaining Actual.
This is only possible because of the generous donations from you the users.
Many of you donate regularly and there are over 8000 Pikapods users whose hosting fees partially go towards supporting Actual.
We offer a very hearty thank you to those who are donating.
See the bottom of the post for ways to support the project if you would like to donate.

## 2026 Wish list

**Plugins**: We have been working on adding plugins to allow users to more easily add functionality to the app without the need to add said feature to the base app.
The feature is not quite ready as plugins have a tendency to break existing features, which slows down development a great deal.
We are doing everything we can to not break existing features that we know you rely on.
Our hope is to have plugins ready for you to build on in the first few months of 2026.

The first plugins we will be adding will be to migrate the existing bank sync providers.
We also are looking at adding multiple new providers soon after.
Multiple prospective providers have reached out to us in just the last few months and are patiently waiting for plugins before fully integrating into Actual.

**Goals UI**: The goal templates and cleanup templates experimental features are used by many, if not most of you.
We plan on getting a proper GUI put together for these to make adding and editing templates less prone to error.
This would also include the ability to predict the total needed to meet all set budget goals, see all active goals, and easily modify fill order.

**Mobile view feature parity**: The mobile view has received many updates this year but it still lacks a number of features that are available on desktop. We would like to bring that disparity down to close to 0 this year.

**Rewrite the transaction table**: The transaction table is probably the most important feature of the app, even more so than the budget itself.
The code for the transaction table is complicated, and not conducive to new features.
We plan to rewrite this code to be more maintainable, more accessible to new contributors, and more extendable for new features such as resizing columns.

**Debt account type**: Currently Actual only has a standard account, you can add transactions and there is a balance.
This is perfect for checking and savings accounts, but less great for loans.
We would like to bring back account types to make more specialty type accounts easier to manage in Actual, starting with loan accounts.
The ability to automate this is technically already available with rules and schedules, but adding in a custom account type that does the setup for you would be that much better.
We will look at what other account types would make sense for the base app, but with plugins the possibilities are endless.

**Better and faster code tests**: We have stared work on upgrading our CI/CD to use Rust based tooling.
This speeds up the tests immensely and makes development and testing faster.

(Remember to vote on the features you would like to see get added to Actual.
Use this link to see [all open feature requests] and vote by reacting with 👍)

Thank you all that contribute!
Whether that be through donations, bug reporting, code submissions, documentation edits, or helping on discord, Actual wouldn't exist without you.

Happy Budgeting and have a happy new year!

entries.title: Fighting AI Slop
entries.body:
Actual has started receiving what can only be described as _AI slop_ — pull requests and issues generated entirely by automated systems with no human involvement. These require the same amount of triage and review time as genuine contributions, but add no value. Every minute spent dealing with machine-generated junk is time not spent improving Actual itself.

## The Problem

To be clear: AI is a useful tool. We use it ourselves to draft code, fix bugs, and build features. Heck - even this article was written with the assistance of AI. But the difference is that a human is always in charge. We review, test, and take responsibility for what we merge. What we are seeing now is the opposite — unreviewed output blindly pushed upstream (i.e. opened as PRs or issues). That is not contribution; it's pollution.

## Our Policy

From this point on, we will close any PRs or issues that appear to be 100% AI-generated with no sign of human oversight. This isn't about being harsh, it's about protecting the limited time our maintainers have to review genuine contributions.

## Why This Matters

Every AI slop PR or issue requires the same triage and review time as genuine contributions. With limited maintainer bandwidth, this directly impacts:

- Response times for real issues and feature requests
- Time available for reviewing legitimate contributions
- Overall project velocity

We want to spend our time improving Actual, not filtering through automated noise.

## How to Contribute Properly with AI

If you're using AI to help with contributions, that's perfectly fine! Just make sure you:

- **Review everything** before submitting, understand what changed and why
- **Test your changes** - don't assume AI-generated code works correctly
- **Respond to feedback** - be ready to discuss, iterate, and improve your contribution
- **Take responsibility** - you're the one submitting it, so make sure it's something you stand behind
- **Tag them with "ai generated"** (This isn't something we can truly enforce, but it's a gesture of good will — it helps everyone in the review process know when AI was involved.)

For more details on how to contribute, see our [contributing guidelines](https://actualbudget.org/docs/contributing).

## A Silver Lining

One small silver lining: our "WIP" (Work-In-Progress) workflow — which requires contributors to manually remove the "WIP" prefix before a PR can be reviewed — has proven effective at filtering out AI bots. It's an unintentional captcha we have built. Many of them can't complete that simple step, so their PRs go stale and close automatically.

Even so, it would be better not to receive AI slop at all.

## Keep It Human

Please, if you're using AI to help contribute, stay in the loop. Review, edit, and understand what you're submitting. Actual is built by humans, for humans. Keep it that way.

We're grateful for all genuine contributions, whether AI-assisted or not. The key is human oversight and understanding. Thank you for helping keep Actual focused on what matters.

entries.title: Continuing to reward contributors
entries.body:
[Three months ago](https://actualbudget.org/blog/spending-community-funds), we launched an experiment: using community donations to directly support the people who keep this project running. The idea was simple — compensate core contributors for the invisible but essential work of reviewing pull requests, triaging issues, and preparing releases.

Today, we're excited to share that the trial has been a success. 🎉

Thanks to your feedback, patience, and ongoing support, we've ironed out the kinks in the system, resolved bugs in the points tracking process, and proven that this model is both fair and sustainable.

As a result: **we're making contributor payments permanent.**

## What This Means

- Core contributors will continue to receive stipends based on their monthly contributions.
- The transparent points system (for PR reviews, issue triage, and releases) remains in place.
- Funding continues to come from our community donations on [OpenCollective].

This ensures that the essential maintenance work — the work that enables everything else to happen — is recognized and supported long-term.

## What's Next: Expanding the System

The initial trial was focused on core maintenance. Now that the foundation is solid, we're preparing to expand. Over the coming months, we plan to introduce:

- **Bug bounties** → Rewards for fixing long-standing or high-impact issues.
- **Feature bounties** → Incentives for implementing important improvements requested by the community.
- **Other initiatives** → Ways to make contributing more rewarding and sustainable for everyone, not just core maintainers.

We'll share details about these expansions soon — so stay tuned!

## Thank You ❤️

This project is powered by generosity, trust, and shared care. By supporting contributors financially, we're not just sustaining the software — we're sustaining the community behind it.

To everyone who has donated, given feedback, or contributed time and energy: thank you. This is your success as much as ours.

entries.title: Proposal for spending community funds
entries.body:
Our open source community has reached an exciting point: thanks to the incredible generosity of our donors, we now have a steady flow of funds coming in. First of all — thank you.

This support allows us to make the project more sustainable for everyone involved. We want to start by addressing something that is often overlooked in open source: the invisible labor that keeps everything running.

We're proposing a 3-month trial program to pay our core maintainers for the essential (but often unglamorous) work of:

- Reviewing pull requests
- Triage and categorize GitHub issues
- Preparing releases

We believe it's time to recognize the financial value of labor — but before we move forward, we want to hear your feedback. Join the conversation on [Discord] or leave anonymous feedback in [this form].

> **Update:** This proposal has been approved. More details about the payment system can be found in the [paying contributors](https://actualbudget.org/docs/contributing/leadership/paying-contributors) page.

## What We're Proposing

Starting July 1st, we'd like to set aside $1,000 per month from the project's funds for a review stipend pool. This pool would be divided between **core maintainers** based on the work they do each month, measured via a transparent points system.

- Points are assigned based on the size of PRs reviewed (using lines of code as a proxy for effort).
- Additional points are awarded for labelling and grooming issues, closing duplicates, and managing releases.
- The system has a cap, and in months with less activity, the payout is reduced to $500.
- Payments are handled via OpenCollective and are only available to core maintainers.

This system is designed to be lightweight, fair, and easy to administer — and it keeps our monthly costs well within our donation income.

## Why Start With Admin Work?

Before we consider feature bounties or bug bounties, we need to acknowledge the day-to-day labor that enables these contributions to be merged and released. Paying for features while leaving critical administrative work unpaid would be unsustainable — and unfair.

This trial serves as the foundation for broader funding efforts in the future. However, it begins with respecting the work that is already being done.

## What We Need From You

We believe this is the right direction — but we won't go ahead without the community's support.

- If you're for it, against it, or have suggestions — let us know.
- If there's strong opposition, we won't implement it.
- If the community supports it, we'll begin the trial in July.

Join the conversation on [Discord] or leave anonymous feedback in [this form].
We're listening — and we'll publish a summary of the feedback before moving forward.

## What's Next?

- We'll collect community feedback until late June.
- If there's consensus, the 3-month trial begins July 1st.
- After the trial, we'll evaluate how it went and where to go next.

---

Thank you again for being part of this journey. This community runs on trust, time, and care. With your feedback, we can keep building something that works — for all of us.
